title: The Paper Bag Princess
author: Robert Munsch

hero.name: Princess Elizabeth
hero.description: Young princess wearing a paper bag, messy hair, determined expression — Robert Munsch character from cover
hero.source_note: Named/distinctive character — source from Creative Fabrica, TPT, or Teachers Pay Teachers clip art; generic Boardmaker princess icon will not show paper bag costume

ambiguous.issue: Could mean a campfire, fireplace, house fire, or the dragon's breath flame
ambiguous.reason: In this book fire refers to the dragon breathing flames and burning Elizabeth's clothes — dragon-breath fire is the correct meaning

ambiguous.issue: Could mean running legs (action) or a running nose etc.
ambiguous.reason: Elizabeth runs to the dragon's cave — physical running action is the correct meaning

ambiguous.issue: Could mean clever/intelligent (adjective) or physical pain (verb: it smarts)
ambiguous.reason: Elizabeth outsmarts the dragon with her clever tricks — intelligent meaning is correct

notes: Key theme of this book is gender-role reversal — Elizabeth rescues the prince, not the other way around. The paper bag costume is central and distinctive; ensure the hero image clearly shows Elizabeth in the brown paper bag, not a traditional princess dress. 'Rescue', 'brave', and 'smart' are critical fringe words because the story's message hinges on Elizabeth's cleverness and courage. 'Burn' covers the dragon destroying the castle and Elizabeth's clothes. Secondary character Prince Ronald does not require a sourced custom image — a generic 'prince' Boardmaker symbol is sufficient. Existing activity_images (princess, prince, dragon, castle, paper bag, forest, fire, crown, cave, smoke) and aac_extras (brave, clever, rescue, roar) provide strong coverage; 'clever' from aac_extras is near-equivalent to 'smart' — consider using 'clever' instead of 'smart' to reuse existing asset.

matching.note: Min 4 approved stems, no hard cap

cvc_decode.note: 3-5 groups x 3 CVC words (phonics, not theme icons)
